a: Molarity is mol/L solution; molality is mol/kg solvent.
Colligative properties depend on particle number, not identity.
Solutes raise boiling point of solvents.
Solutes lower freezing point of solvents.
Osmotic pressure relates to solute concentration.
Rate laws express rate in terms of concentrations and constants.
Order is the exponent sum in an experimental rate law.
Half-life formulas depend on reaction order.
Catalysts provide alternate pathways with lower activation energy.
Pressure changes shift gas equilibria toward fewer/more moles.
